draft.title: Conservation of energy and efficiency
card: Energy changes from one form to another but is not created or destroyed. The total energy stays the same.
Some energy usually ends up as thermal energy that spreads into the surroundings. It is not lost, but it is not useful for the task.
Power is the rate of energy transfer: P = E ÷ t. It is measured in watts (W), where 1 W is 1 J each second.
Efficiency is the share of input energy that becomes useful output. Efficiency = useful output ÷ total input, often written as a percentage.
draft.remember: Energy is never lost, but only the useful share counts toward efficiency.

a.q: A motor takes in 500 J of energy and gives out 350 J of useful energy. What is its efficiency?
a.why: Efficiency = 350 ÷ 500 = 0.70, or 70%. The 30% figure is the share wasted as thermal energy, not the useful share.
a.clue: Divide the useful output by the total input.

b.q: Nina's kettle transfers 180 000 J of electrical energy in 90 s. What is its power?
b.why: Power = energy ÷ time = 180 000 ÷ 90 = 2000 W. Multiplying the two numbers gives a far larger value, but power is a rate, so it needs division by the time.
b.clue: Power is energy transferred each second.

problems.detail: Why (a) says the remaining 30% is all wasted as thermal energy. The question does not say this, and the card says only that wasted energy 'usually' ends up as thermal energy; some could be sound or other forms. It would be better to say the 30% is the share that is not useful (mostly thermal energy).

check.summary: Both questions are correct and suit Year 11. One small issue: the why for (a) states that all the wasted 30% is thermal energy, which is more definite than the card's 'usually'.
